data.title: CG Oncology Shares Rise on Third Quarter Beat
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

CG Oncology shares were higher after the company's third-quarter revenue and loss per share came in better than expected.

The stock climbed 20% to $77.96 on Friday. Shares are up 87% this year.

The cancer treatment developer logged a loss of $56.9 million, or 64 cents a share, compared with a loss of $43.8 million, or 57 cents a share, the year before. The loss was narrower than the 84 cents a share that Wall Street was projecting.

Revenue was $1.6 million, down from $1.7 million the year before. That was ahead of the $500,000 analysts had expected.

CG Oncology expects to share data from studies in November and December. It had also added Isabel Kalofonos as Chief Commercial Officer in October.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: Boeing said to deliver 32 MAX jets in October, fewest in nearly a year
data.description:
Boeing delivered ~32 of its 737 MAX jets in October, the fewest in nearly a year, Bloomberg reported Friday, in a blow to the planemaker's efforts to boost cash flow and improve its finances.

The decline in October deliveries, based on Cirium data and an analyst note by Sheila Kahyaoglu of Jefferies, compared with September’s 43 jets, would mark the smallest number since last November.

The final quarter of the year typically sees higher deliveries from plane manufacturers as they work to meet annual guidance targets.

Boeing warned last week that it would take longer than expected to increase 737 MAX production and would be unable to meet its previous target of delivering 500 commercial aircraft in 2026.

data.title: Nubank, Mercado Pago halt crypto transfers after external provider disruption
data.description:
Brazilian digital lender Nubank and Mercado Pago, the fintech arm from MercadoLibre , have halted some cryptocurrency transfers due to disruptions from an external data provider, the companies said in separate statements on Friday.

  • Nubank said it has halted cryptocurrency withdrawals and deposits

  • Mercado Pago said it blocked some transfers to external wallets, and added that deposits could also face delays

  • Both companies said client funds remain secure, and that other crypto products continue to operate as usual

  • Neither company identified the external provider involved, and it was unclear whether both were affected by the same provider

  • Nubank cited "instability from an external data provider," while Mercado Pago mentioned "an incident affecting a risk monitoring and anti-money laundering service provider"

  • Last week, hackers targeted exchange Binance to drain $6.3 billion worth of crypto, the largest such heist on record

data.title: Chip Stocks Rebound After Rout — WSJ
data.description:
By Robbie Whelan

What goes down, sometimes comes right back up. Chip stocks, which fell sharply Thursday, have bounced back Friday as the market stabilized following a historic tech rout triggered by election results and rising anxieties over artificial intelligence.

The PHLX Semiconductor index, which tracks the 30 largest names in the design, manufacturing and distribution of microchips, was recently up 3.7%.

Nearly every major stock in the sector rose. Nvidia shares were up 3.3%, Advanced Micro Devices 9%, Micron Technology 6%, Intel 7%, Qualcomm 5%, Broadcom 1% and Marvell Technology 4%.

Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya wrote Friday that "indiscriminate selling of chip stocks on AI capex fears could start to run its course" by early 2027. The bank predicted that expected clarity from local and state governments on data center regulations would help stabilize the market, and said that moderate cuts to capital expenditures could even help companies regain their bearings by leading to capacity constraints and price increases, driving sales higher.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Zylox-Tonbridge and GL Capital Announce Strategic Investment in LifeTech Scientific to Build a Leading Vascular and Structural Heart Intervention Platform
data.description:
HANGZHOU, China, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zylox-Tonbridge Medical Technology Co., Ltd. () ("Zylox-Tonbridge") today announced a strategic investment in LifeTech Scientific Corporation () ("LifeTech"), in partnership with GL Capital, marking a significant step toward building a leading integrated vascular and structural heart intervention platform in China.

The investment is expected to bring together Zylox-Tonbridge's peripheral vascular and neurovascular businesses with LifeTech's aortic and structural heart businesses, creating a comprehensive portfolio across four key therapeutic areas. The companies also aim to leverage their complementary R&D capabilities and global commercial networks to accelerate innovation and expand their international reach.

Under the agreement, Zylox-Tonbridge and GL Capital will jointly invest approximately HK$1.482 billion in LifeTech through GL Lighthouse Two Investment Limited ("Lighthouse Two"), which will subscribe for newly issued shares representing approximately 16.7% of LifeTech's enlarged share capital. Upon completion, Lighthouse Two will become LifeTech's largest single shareholder, with Zylox-Tonbridge holding a 60% stake in Lighthouse Two through an investment of approximately HK$889 million.

In a related transaction, GL Capital will subscribe for 39.8 million newly issued Zylox-Tonbridge shares at HK$22 per share, representing approximately 10.8% of the company's enlarged issued share capital. The subscription price represents a 13.5% premium to the closing share price on the announcement date and a 15.4% premium to the average closing price over the preceding five trading days, reflecting GL Capital's confidence in Zylox-Tonbridge's long-term prospects. The proceeds will support Zylox-Tonbridge's potential future investments in LifeTech and international business development.

Beyond the investment, Zylox-Tonbridge and GL Capital may acquire additional shares in LifeTech to support closer collaboration and business growth. Zylox-Tonbridge also intends to pursue a potential merger with LifeTech, with the aim of building a leading integrated vascular and structural heart intervention platform in China.

Bringing Together Complementary Strengths Across Four Therapeutic Areas

LifeTech is a leading medical device company in China specializing in cardio-cerebrovascular and peripheral vascular interventions, with an established position in aortic and structural heart interventions. The company has developed a comprehensive portfolio of endovascular solutions for complex aortic diseases, including aortic arch and branch vessel reconstruction. Its structural heart portfolio includes the LAmbre™ and LAxible™ left atrial appendage occluders and three generations of congenital heart defect occluders.

LifeTech has also developed several first-in-class products, including the G-Branch™ thoracoabdominal aortic stent graft system, Concave Supra-arch branched stent-graft system and SureCham™ aortic arch single branch stent graft system. The company holds more than 50 medical device registration certificates in China, with 20 products accepted into China's special review procedure for innovative medical devices. As of June 30, 2026, LifeTech had filed 2,608 valid patent applications, including 1,370 valid granted patents.

Zylox-Tonbridge brings complementary expertise in peripheral vascular and neurovascular interventions through its two brands, Zylox Medical and Tonbridge Medical. The company is one of the few in China offering comprehensive product solutions across both areas, with strong R&D, manufacturing and commercialization capabilities. Since the beginning of 2025, six additional Zylox-Tonbridge products have been accepted into China's special review procedure for innovative medical devices. The company now serves more than 3,500 hospitals across China.

The strategic investment is expected to help both companies expand their businesses and strengthen their market positions.

Strengthening the Global Competitiveness of Chinese MedTech Brands

The companies' established international commercial networks offer further opportunities for collaboration and market expansion.

Zylox-Tonbridge reported a 349.3% year-over-year increase in revenue from markets outside Mainland China in the first half of 2026. The company has commercialized its products in over 70 countries and regions outside Mainland China, supported by a distribution network covering more than 135 countries and regions.

Zylox-Tonbridge has strengthened its local operations in Europe through the acquisition and integration of Germany-based vascular intervention company optimed. The company continues to expand its presence across key markets in Europe, Latin America and Asia.

LifeTech also has an established international presence, with seven subsidiaries outside Mainland China and a sales network spanning nearly 120 countries and regions. In 2025, its revenue from markets outside Mainland China reached nearly RMB400 million, up approximately 14.4% year over year and accounting for nearly 30% of total revenue. Europe and Asia were its primary international revenue contributors.

The strategic investment is expected to create opportunities for the companies to leverage their complementary product portfolios, commercial networks and operating capabilities, strengthening the competitiveness of Chinese MedTech brands in international markets.

Leadership Perspectives

Dr. Jonathon Zhong Zhao, Chairman of Zylox-Tonbridge, said:

"This strategic investment marks an important milestone in our ambition to build a leading integrated vascular and structural heart intervention platform in China. By combining our strengths in peripheral and neurovascular interventions with LifeTech's expertise in aortic and structural heart interventions, we aim to establish a more comprehensive portfolio and create new opportunities for long-term growth.

"With our established operating capabilities and expanding global presence, we see significant opportunities to capture synergies, strengthen our competitiveness and advance our growth as a global medical technology company."

Mr. Zhenfu Li, Founder, Managing Partner and Chief Executive Officer of GL Capital, said:

"GL Capital has long been committed to supporting leading healthcare companies in China through long-term investment and strategic support. We see significant potential in China's vascular intervention market and the global growth prospects of innovative Chinese medical technology companies.

"This strategic investment provides an opportunity to bring together complementary resources and advance our shared goal of building a globally competitive vascular and structural heart intervention platform. We will continue to leverage our capital and industry resources to strengthen the companies' competitiveness and support their global expansion."

Mr. Yuehui Xie, Founder of LifeTech Scientific, said:

"This strategic investment reflects strong confidence in LifeTech's innovation capabilities, market position and long-term growth potential. Zylox-Tonbridge and LifeTech have highly complementary businesses, product portfolios and commercial networks, creating opportunities for closer collaboration and greater synergies.

"The investment marks a new chapter for LifeTech, with the potential to strengthen our competitive position through closer collaboration in products, technologies and resources. As Senior Advisor, I will continue to contribute my nearly three decades of industry experience to LifeTech's long-term development, with a deep personal commitment to the company's continued growth and success."

About Zylox-Tonbridge

Zylox-Tonbridge Medical Technology Co., Ltd. () is a leading vascular intervention medical technology company in China, focused on the research, development, manufacturing and global commercialization of innovative medical devices. Its brands include Zylox Medical and Tonbridge Medical, which specialize in peripheral vascular and neurovascular interventions, respectively.

Zylox-Tonbridge has established a comprehensive portfolio of innovative products, with 69 products approved by China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) as of August 2026. Its products are commercialized in 70 countries and regions outside Mainland China. Listed on the HKEX in 2021, the company is pursuing its strategy to build a globally competitive vascular and structural heart intervention platform.

About GL Capital

GL Capital is a China-focused healthcare investment firm founded in 2010 by Jeffery Li, former President of Novartis China. The firm specializes in healthcare buyout and growth investments and manages more than RMB30 billion in assets across U.S. dollar- and RMB-denominated private equity, venture capital and hedge funds.

GL Capital focuses on investments in healthcare companies with sustainable competitive advantages and works with management teams to support long-term business development and value creation.

About LifeTech Scientific

Established in 1999 in Shenzhen, China, LifeTech Scientific Corporation () specializes in the research, development, manufacturing and commercialization of minimally invasive interventional medical devices for cardio-cerebrovascular and peripheral vascular diseases.

The company has established a comprehensive product portfolio in aortic and structural heart interventions and developed the world's first iron-based bioabsorbable material technology platform. LifeTech maintains leading market positions in China for its key products and was among the first Chinese medical device companies to achieve large-scale international commercialization of high-value medical devices. Its global sales network spans nearly 120 countries and regions, supported by more than 1,000 distributors.

SOURCE ZYLOX-TONBRIDGE

data.title: The Week in Oil: Crude Falls Below $100 a Barrel Amid U.S. Midterms Shake-up
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni

Here is a look at what happened in oil markets in the week of Nov. 2-6 and what the focus will be in the days to come.

OVERVIEW: Oil prices are poised for a staggering weekly loss of 14% after a volatile week, as markets await Washington's next move on Iran following the U.S. midterms. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, traded around $97 a barrel on Friday, while West Texas Intermediate was at $90 a barrel. "Confidence has returned to the oil market," analysts at Commerzbank said. "If diplomatic efforts appear promising, oil prices could even fall somewhat further."

GEOPOLITICAL RISKS: The oil market witnessed a sharp selloff this week, driven by growing hopes for a diplomatic solution between the U.S. and Iran after the Democratic sweep of Congress during the U.S. elections and President Trump's acknowledgment that the war contributed to widespread Republican losses. However, any change in Washington's balance of power will take time to translate into policy.

Traders now fear that the Trump administration could launch a fresh military attack on Iran, which could trigger retaliation from the Iranian regime against energy infrastructure in the region. Meanwhile, a sustained recovery in oil flows from the Middle East remains at risk due to attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and threats by Yemen's Houthi militants against Saudi Arabia and its Red Sea export route.

"The risk of renewed escalation is by no means off the table," said Barbara Lambrecht, analyst at Commerzbank. "For one thing, attacks in the Strait of Hormuz have continued unabated. For another, the positions of the parties to the conflict remain far apart in the talks."

SUPPLY AND DEMAND: Physical oil prices are signaling an easing in global supply conditions, despite continued threats to shipping. Some analysts say recovering Middle East exports and weaker demand are pushing the market back toward surplus, with high prices weighing on consumption. J.P. Morgan estimates that supply exceeded demand by 1.1 million barrels a day in September, with the surplus widening to 1.4 million barrels a day in October.

Diesel prices have followed crude lower, but there is still persistent tightness in middle-distillate supplies. U.S. inventories of diesel and heating oil fell to their lowest in more than two decades last week, according to the Energy Information Administration. Meanwhile, supply risks remain elevated amid persistent Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian refineries, casting doubt on Moscow's plans to increase diesel exports towards year-end.

Meanwhile, against the backdrop of recovering supply, major Persian Gulf oil producers are offering significant discounts on their crude to offset elevated tanker and freight costs. State oil company Saudi Aramco on Thursday cut the official selling price for December shipments of its Arab Light crude to Asia--the largest market for Middle Eastern oil--by $2 a barrel to a discount of $7 a barrel to the Oman/Dubai benchmark. "The discount on December deliveries of Arab Light to Asia is now almost as large as it was during the Covid pandemic six and a half years ago," analysts at Commerzbank said.

WHAT'S AHEAD: The International Energy Agency, the EIA and the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries are set to release their latest oil-market reports next week, with investors looking for further signs of an easing in physical market conditions.

OPEC's report will be closely watched for production figures, while the IEA's latest inventory data will be a key focus. The figures are expected to point to a continued slowdown in stock drawdowns, with recent declines in OECD inventories driven largely by government reserve withdrawals, while commercial stocks have started to rebuild, according to analysts.

China's trade data will also be in focus, with crude-oil imports expected to have risen further in October, reflecting increased supplies from the Gulf region,

On the U.S. economic calendar, markets will watch for inflation data, with the consumer-price index due on Tuesday and the producer-price index on Friday. Investors will also focus on weekly jobless claims on Thursday and a series of Federal Reserve appearances for clues on the outlook for interest rates.

Write to Giulia Petroni at giulia.petroni@wsj.com

data.title: Bears charge, bulls retreat in AAII's latest sentiment survey
data.description:
Key points:
  • All three major US stock indexes green; Nasdaq out front
  • Tech leads S&P 500 sector gainers; consumer staples down most
  • Dollar up; US crude, gold down; bitcoin turns positive
  • US 10-yr Treasury yield up at 4.85%

BEARS CHARGE, BULLS RETREAT IN AAII'S LATEST SENTIMENT SURVEY

Individual investors have taken a pessimistic turn, according to the American Association of Individual Investors' (AAII) most recent sentiment survey.

The results show bearish sentiment—or expectations that stock prices will fall over the next six months—leapt 6.9 percentage points to 48.4%, coasting above its long-term historical average of 31.5% for the 39th consecutive week.

The bulls—who believe stock prices will rise in the next six months—retreated 3.7 percentage points to 34.1%, landing below their 37.5% historical average for the second time in three weeks.

The neutral camp—which sees no change in stock prices between now and May—shrank by 3.2 percentage points to 17.5%. AAII calls the reading "unusually low" and points out that neutral sentiment has now been south of its historic level of 31.0% for the 35th straight week.

Taken together, the bull-bear spread (bullish minus bearish) narrowed by 10.7 percentage points to -14.3%, lurking below its 6.5% long-term average for the 16th consecutive week.

AAII's special question to its members this week asked survey participants what they thought of the US Federal Reserve's decision to leave its key interest rate unchanged last week.

The majority (55.5%) said it was the right move, while 30.7% said the central bank should have hiked rates. The "they should have cut rates" camp accounted for 6.6% of the respondents. The remaining 7.3% were unsure or had no opinion on the matter.

data.title: Canadian dollar hits nearly three-week low on surprise jobs loss
data.description:
By Fergal Smith

The Canadian dollar fell to a nearly three-week low against its US counterpart on Friday after domestic data showed the economy shed jobs for a third straight month, cooling expectations for Bank of Canada interest rate hikes.

The loonie was trading 0.7% lower at 1.4110 per US dollar, or 70.87 US cents, after touching its weakest intraday level since October 19 at 1.4125.

  • For the week, the currency was on track to lose nearly 1%, after three straight weeks of gains, as equity markets globally were buffeted by a selloff in AI stocks.

  • "The CAD has failed to deliver on the potential for its recent rebound to extend this week," Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret, FX strategists at Scotiabank, said in a note.

  • "Elevated equity-market volatility has overshadowed pretty much everything else, although the combination of weak Canadian and strong US jobs data has given the CAD an added nudge lower into the weekend," the strategists said.

  • Canadian employment fell 4,700 in October and the jobless rate rose to a six-month high of 6.7%. Analysts had expected a 13,600 jobs gain.

  • Chances the Bank of Canada would tighten in December dipped to 35% from 40%, swap market data showed.

  • The Canadian central bank unveiled on Thursday a new five-year monetary policy framework with the federal finance ministry, keeping its inflation target unchanged at 2%.

  • Also on Thursday, Prime Minister Mark Carney's budget showed that he plans to use windfall oil revenue to boost Canada's productivity and build infrastructure while keeping his previous fiscal goals intact.

  • US nonfarm payrolls increased more than expected in October, boosting the US dollar against a basket of major currencies.

  • US crude futures CLc1 added to their steep weekly decline, trading 0.1% lower at $90.40 a barrel, after the election losses of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party raised hopes of a de-escalation in the US-Israeli war on Iran. Oil is one of Canada's major exports.

data.title: Ubiquiti Shares Gain on Higher 1Q Profit, Revenue
data.description:
By Connor Hart

Shares of Ubiquiti climbed after the company reported sharply higher profit and revenue in the recent quarter.

The stock rose 17%, to $599.88, on Friday. Shares are up nearly 6% year to date.

The company before the bell reported a fiscal first-quarter profit of $320.5 million, or $5.29 a share, up from $207.9 million, or $3.43 a share, a year earlier.

Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted earnings came in at $5.32 a share.

Revenue rose 40% to $1.03 billion. The company attributed the gain to growth in both its enterprise-technology and service-provider-technology platforms.

Enterprise-technology revenue jumped 43% to $941.3 million, while service-provider-technology revenue climbed 11% to $84.9 million.

Ubiquiti said it continues to face higher costs and supply-chain constraints for certain components, warning that the trends may result in near-term pressure on margins and inventory.
